reason_for_new_version: The v1 protocol preceded the generic checked runtime, referred to updates not yet produced, and used the eight-case learning domain where the implemented comparison now separates a four-case declared current domain from a nonempty exact future request.
scientific_scope: Capacity comparison on one exact learned artifact family and one exact pair of proof-free updates. This protocol is neither a universal impossibility claim nor a practical performance claim.
same_material_rules: Every adapter receives the byte-identical learned artifact and the exact aligned/bypass candidate pair.
Current behavior is evaluated on exactly the four inputs enumerated by learnedRuntimeDeclaredCurrentDomain.
Future behavior is evaluated on exactly the nonempty request list learnedOperationalCounterfactualRequests.
An adapter may expose less evidence than the constitutive runtime, but it may not replace the artifact, candidate, intent, domain, future request or target contract.
A baseline-specific summary is never accepted as a substitute for the shared serialized material.

capability_status_vocabulary.certified: A checked theorem or certificate establishes the capability for the exact shared material.
capability_status_vocabulary.observed: The frozen executable adapter returns direct evidence on the exact shared material, without a theorem claim.
capability_status_vocabulary.not-certified: The adapter ran but supplied no certificate of the capability; this does not assert impossibility or absence.
capability_status_vocabulary.out-of-interface: The frozen baseline interface does not express the capability; this does not assert impossibility or absence.
capability_status_vocabulary.adapter-unavailable: No frozen executable adapter exists; no comparative conclusion is permitted.

subject.interface: one initial CheckedAgent plus proof-free serialized updates submitted through the closed submitUpdate API
subject.required_evidence: one dependent executed chain on the exact shared material, reporting all eight capabilities separately

baselines.interface: candidate artifact times complete declared current domain to output table and verdict
fixed candidate artifact times declared intervention basis to causal observation report
baselines.comparison_output: causal dependencies on the exact candidate without runtime installation

baselines.interface: candidate action times current policy state to allow or refuse before effect
baselines.comparison_output: pre-effect action decision on each exact candidate

baselines.interface: certified current system times proof-free proposed update times invariant to certified successor or rejection
checked source artifact times serialized delta times source certificate to checked target certificate or rejection
baselines.comparison_output: transported and recomputed certificate fragments plus exact target verdict

baselines.interface: finite proof-free update trace times initial checked runtime to dependent checked history or first rejection
baselines.comparison_output: certificate and installation status at every reached version

extensional_limitation.scope: verifiers whose verdict factors exclusively through the complete declared current table
extensional_limitation.forbidden_generalization: No limitation is inferred for verifiers that consume causal, historical, future or contract-indexed material.

pre_registered_decision_rules: No baseline row may be emitted before its executable adapter, command and source hashes are frozen in a new adapter manifest.
The confirmatory run must execute every frozen adapter on the exact shared material in one run.
Missing adapters and out-of-interface capabilities are never negative results.
Certified, observed and not-certified are reported separately and never collapsed into one score.
No result may infer a universal impossibility from one baseline implementation.
The extensional limitation may be reported only at its stated factorization boundary.
Timing and resource measurements, if later added, require a separately versioned protocol and cannot be inserted into this capacity protocol.
Any change to a shared object, baseline interface, capability, decision rule or result schema requires a new protocol version.
